content: Salicylic acid (SA) plays a critical role as a signaling molecule in plant defense mechanisms. A specific SA-response element (SARE) has been identified within the tobacco PR2-d gene. A 76 base pair (bp) DNA fragment associated with this SARE was shown to induce a 20-fold increase in gene expression in transgenic tobacco plants when exposed to SA. Protein binding studies have further revealed that the core sequence of this SARE is TTCGACCTCC. The content provided here was originally contributed by Henry A. Hoff. Some of the initial material for this page was derived from Wikiversity.
